reader.requirement: A format 2 READ of an indexed file with KEY IS data-name-1 (prime or alternate, random or dynamic access) must retrieve by that key, and under dynamic access every later format 1 READ NEXT must walk that key until another key of reference is established.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly (ChangedIn 2002): at 85 a random READ of an alternate key whose next record duplicates it sets I-O status 02 (§1985:IX.1.3.4 GRL2.1); the key-of-reference assignment and record selection are not under the switch
the compiling program's edition baked on the connector, read by every DialectBehaviors.IsActive in the connector
DialectBehavior.IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd, guarded by 'previous &&': only READ PREVIOUS after OPEN; a NEXT walk at 85 takes the same code as 2023
Edition.Year < 2002: a dynamic-access READ with AT END but no NEXT is refused (§1985:IX.4.5.3 SR5); 2002+ imply NEXT

reader.edition-search: read KeyedIoBinder.BindRead, KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead and the IndexedConnector READ members; grep DialectBehaviors.IsActive|Edition|Year|DialectLevel over those files and the StatementValidation READ checks
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the key of reference (ReadRandom assigns _refKey = keyIndex at every edition and the walk reads _refKey); yes for the status only: at 85 the random alternate READ answers 02 when a duplicate follows, at 2023 00
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf29_05 covers dynamic access with a unique alternate; not covered: random access KEY IS alternate, KEY IS the prime key written explicitly, an alternate WITH DUPLICATES as key of reference for the following READ NEXTs, a failed keyed READ

probes.expected: after READ KEY IS R-ALT the READ NEXTs follow alternate order (02, 09, then CC's 07); KEY IS R-KEY makes the prime key the reference again (07 then 09); a failed READ leaves no valid next record (GR12, GR4a)

probes.expected: random access retrieves by the named key's value, not the prime key's

reader.notes: ReadRandom sets _refKey to the bound KEY phrase's key index before the lookup; ReadSequential/SelectSequentialRecord seek in _refKey's tree, so the key persists for READ NEXT under dynamic access. Probed unique and duplicate alternates, random and dynamic access, and the 2023 contrast.

refuter.evidence: Probes run at --std 85 through run_case.py under refute-1985-097/. q1keyref-002 (dynamic access, two alternates): READ KEY IS R-U OF R (qualified, SR3) gave Q1=00 02BBu2w2nd. A WRITE in between left R-U as the key of reference: Q2=00 03ZZu3w6th, Q3=00 05BBu5w1st. A REWRITE left it too: Q5=00 09BBu9w3rd. After a failed KEY IS R-U: X1 INV 23, X2=46 (GR12). q2seq-002 (sequential access, START on the alternate): the walk stays on R-ALT. q8mix-001: KEY IS with NEXT or AT END is refused (COBOL2269). q5refuse-001: KEY IS R-DAT, a non-key, is refused (COBOL0864, SR2), and so is KEY on a relative file. IndexedConnector.ReadRandom sets _refKey = keyIndex before the lookup, and SelectSequentialRecord seeks in _refKey's tree. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR15; OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR12. Side note, not this rule: COBOL0864 cites §2023:14.9.30.3 SR10/SR11 at --std 85.
